In the Professional Summary, change the opening to explicitly match the role's platform language while retaining only supported claims: "Data engineer with 9 years of experience designing, building and operating production batch and streaming data platforms and cloud data warehouses across logistics, payments and retail." Keep the existing technology and reliability sentence, and add: "Experienced in optimising large-scale warehouse workloads, data quality and dimensional modelling." 2. In the Senior Data Engineer section under Lukovac Freight Hub, revise the first bullet to make operational ownership more ATS-visible: "Own ingestion and orchestration for a production data platform, including approximately 140 Airflow DAGs loading data from PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake; participate in the data-platform on-call rotation one week in six." This uses evidence already present in the candidate notes and improves alignment with the responsibility to run a central platform.
3. In the Senior Data Engineer section under Lukovac Freight Hub, add the supported query-optimisation and scale evidence to the dbt or Snowflake bullet. For example, revise the dbt bullet to: "Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to dbt, building over 420 models with tests on every model; introduced incremental models and slim CI in GitHub Actions, reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5h 10m to 1h 35m." Then revise the Snowflake bullet to: "Reduced monthly Snowflake costs by approximately 37% through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables." This makes the existing optimisation evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to identify without claiming unsupported query techniques.
4. In the Skills section, change "Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling, data contracts, data quality testing" to "Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling (star schema), data contracts, data quality testing, JSON Schema". The star-schema wording is supported by the Redshift warehouse experience, and JSON Schema is explicitly documented in the data-contract achievement.
5. In the Open Source and Community section, retain the Airflow provider contribution but include the technologies from the original candidate material: "Contributed two merged pull requests to a community Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug and adding Python tests." This strengthens the job's open-source-practices match while remaining concise.

job_description_info.job_description:
# Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform

**Company:** Halden Pay (fictional name; cross-border business payments)
**Location:** Lisbon, Portugal (hybrid, 3 days per week in the office)
**Team:** Data Platform

## The role

Halden Pay is growing quickly, and data sits at the centre of that plan. We are looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join the Data Platform team. The team builds and runs the shared data platform that analysts, data scientists and product teams rely on, with a focus on reusable frameworks rather than one-off pipelines.

## Responsibilities

- Own the design, build and day-to-day running of the company's central data platform
- Evaluate and introduce new open-source tools where they bring a clear benefit
- Work with data scientists, analytics engineers and BI colleagues to turn their needs into platform features
- Define and enforce data quality standards, governance rules and access policies

## Tech stack

- Cloud: Google Cloud (BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE)
- Orchestration and transformation: Airflow, dbt
- Engineering: Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, Git

## Requirements

- Experience designing, building and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale
- Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
- Strong data modelling skills (dimensional modelling; graph modelling is a plus)
- Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud (managed warehouse, serverless compute, containers)
- Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
- Good professional English; Portuguese is a plus

If you meet most but not all of the points above, you are still welcome to apply.

## Benefits

- Base salary plus annual bonus
- Training and certification budget
- Support for open-source contributions
- Hybrid work from a central Lisbon office

LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer
Rijeka, Croatia (open to remote, EU time zones) | lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example

PROFILE
Data engineer with 9 years of experience building batch and streaming data platforms for e-commerce and payments. I like boring, well-tested pipelines, clear data contracts and warehouses that analysts actually trust.

EXPERIENCE

Senior Data Engineer - Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. (logistics marketplace), Rijeka            03/2022 - present
- Own the ingestion layer of the company data platform: ~140 Airflow DAGs loading from Postgres, MySQL, Salesforce and 3rd-party APIs into Snowflake.
- Moved transformation logic from stored procedures to dbt (420+ models, tests on every model); nightly run time down from 5h10 to 1h35.
- Introduced data contracts between product teams and the data team (JSON Schema + CI checks), cutting broken-pipeline incidents from ~9/month to ~2/month.
- Built a Kafka-based event pipeline (Kafka Connect + Snowpipe Streaming) for shipment tracking events, ~30M events/day.
- Mentor two mid-level data engineers; run the weekly data platform office hours.

Data Engineer - Kovalent Pay (payments startup), Zagreb                            09/2019 - 02/2022
- Built PySpark jobs on AWS EMR for transaction reconciliation (daily ~1.2 TB of raw files from S3).
- Designed the Redshift warehouse schema (star schema, 30+ fact/dimension tables) used by finance and risk.
- Set up data quality checks with Great Expectations on critical finance tables.
- Wrote internal Python library for S3/Glue catalog access used by 4 teams.

Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer - Adria Retail Group, Split                     06/2017 - 08/2019
- Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL into an on-prem SQL Server warehouse.
- Built Power BI reports for store operations (40+ stores).
- Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron.

EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science (Data Science track) - Northgate Technical University, 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries

SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data: Airflow, dbt, Spark (PySpark), Kafka, Kafka Connect, Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Great Expectations
Cloud & infra: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub Actions
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)

LANGUAGES
Croatian (native), English (C1), German (B1)
candidate_text.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team at Kovalent Pay,

I am applying for the Data Engineer position advertised on your careers page.

For the past two years I have been working at Adria Retail Group, where I started as a BI developer and gradually took over most of our ETL work. The biggest project I delivered was moving 60 nightly SSIS packages to Python scripts, which made our loads easier to debug and to change. Before that, every change to a package needed the one colleague who knew SSIS well.

I want to move from retail BI into a product company where data is closer to the core of the business. Payments are a good fit: reconciliation, fraud and reporting all depend on data being correct and on time, and that is the part of the job I enjoy most. I have been learning Spark in my free time and completed a small project processing public transaction-like datasets with PySpark.

I hold an MSc in Computer Science from Northgate Technical University, where my thesis was about incremental materialized views.

I would be glad to talk about how I could help your data team.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

company_info.company_description:
Halden Pay is a financial technology company providing business accounts, foreign-exchange risk management and trade finance to exporters.

Its stated values are **Together, Ownership and Pace**: sharing information and supporting colleagues across teams, taking responsibility for problems and learning from them, and reducing complexity to move quickly for clients. The company describes a collaborative environment with clear career paths, annual learning budgets and mentoring in every department.

Most offices operate a hybrid model, with three days a week in the office. Engineering teams are organised around payments, risk, data platforms and client experience. Regular team events help build connections across approximately 40 offices.

Employee reviews describe a commercially driven culture with friendly colleagues, though some say onboarding and training vary considerably between teams.

cv_history.content:
LENA VARGA-HOLM
Senior Data Engineer
lena.vargaholm@example.com | +385 55 555 0101 | github.com/lvh-data-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data engineer with 9 years of experience building and operating batch and streaming data platforms across logistics, payments and retail. Experienced in Python, SQL, Airflow, dbt, Kafka and cloud data warehouses, with a focus on reliable pipelines, data quality and dimensional modelling. AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. | 03/2022–Present
- Own ingestion and orchestration for the data platform, including approximately 140 Airflow DAGs loading data from PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake. Participate in the platform on-call rotation, one week in six.
- Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to dbt, building over 420 models with tests on every model. Introduced incremental models and slim CI in GitHub Actions, reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5h 10m to 1h 35m.
- Introduced data contracts using JSON Schema and CI checks between product and data teams, reducing broken-pipeline incidents from approximately nine to two per month.
- Designed and built a Kafka and Snowpipe Streaming pipeline for shipment events, processing approximately 30 million events per day with p95 end-to-end latency under two minutes. Added a dead-letter topic and replay tooling for failed events.
- Replaced hourly full-table extracts of the orders database with Debezium CDC into Kafka, reducing replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
- Reduced monthly Snowflake costs by approximately 37% through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables.
- Mentor two data engineers and run weekly data platform office hours.

Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay | 09/2019–02/2022
- Built PySpark reconciliation jobs on AWS EMR processing approximately 1.2 TB of raw files daily from S3. Automated matching of bank settlement files to internal ledgers, reducing finance's manual reconciliation work from approximately three days to four hours per month-end.
- Designed a dimensional Redshift warehouse with more than 30 fact and dimension tables used by finance and risk.
- Set up Great Expectations data quality checks on critical finance tables.
- Developed an internal Python library for S3 and Glue Data Catalog access, used by four teams.

Junior Data Engineer / BI Developer | Adria Retail Group | 06/2017–08/2019
- Maintained SSIS packages and T-SQL ETL for an on-premises SQL Server warehouse.
- Migrated 60 nightly SSIS jobs to Python scripts scheduled with cron, making loads easier to debug and change.
- Built Power BI reports for store operations across more than 40 stores.

SKILLS
Languages: Python, SQL, Bash
Data platforms: Airflow, dbt, Spark (PySpark), Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Snowflake, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Great Expectations
Cloud and engineering: AWS (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, IAM, MSK), Docker, Terraform (basic), GitHub Actions, CI/CD
Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling, data contracts, data quality testing
BI: Power BI, Looker (basic)

CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024

EDUCATION
MSc Computer Science, Data Science track | Northgate Technical University | 2017
Thesis: Incremental materialized views for analytical queries

OPEN SOURCE AND COMMUNITY
- Contributed two merged pull requests to a community Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug and adding tests in Python.
- Teach beginner SQL at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year since 2021.
- Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup in 2024.

LANGUAGES
Croatian: Native | English: C1 | German: B1

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured senior data engineering CV with clear progression, relevant technical breadth, and unusually effective quantified achievements. It demonstrates production ownership, platform scale, reliability, cost optimisation, data quality, mentoring, and open-source activity. The experience bullets are specific and credible, and the certification, community work, and English proficiency strengthen the profile. Minor opportunities remain to make the fit for a shared Data Platform role even more explicit, particularly around query optimisation, platform operations, and collaboration with analytics or product stakeholders.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, searchable technology names, and no apparent tables, graphics, headers, or parsing obstacles. Strong matching terms include data platform, Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, Kafka, Snowflake, AWS, Spark, Docker, CI/CD, dimensional modelling, data quality, and open source. AI screening probability is high because the document contains both relevant keywords and measurable evidence. To improve matching further, use the job ad's supported wording such as "production data platform," "cloud data warehouse," "query optimisation," and "platform operations" where the existing evidence supports those terms.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with the role. It clearly shows experience designing, building, and operating a production data platform and cloud data warehouses at scale; AWS provides comparable cloud experience to Google Cloud; and the CV demonstrates Airflow, dbt, Python, SQL, Docker, CI/CD, data quality, dimensional modelling, mentoring, and open-source contribution. The payments experience and reconciliation work are particularly relevant to Halden Pay. The platform's data contracts, CI checks, data quality tests, and office hours also support the company's Ownership, Together, and learning-oriented culture, without making unsupported cultural claims. The candidate's material does not show graph modelling or Portuguese, which are nice-to-have gaps. Query optimisation is supported indirectly through the dbt, incremental-model, warehouse-build, and Snowflake cost work, but the CV does not state it explicitly. Access-policy ownership and direct Google Cloud experience are not shown; AWS is the truthful comparable-cloud evidence.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, change the opening to explicitly match the role's platform language while retaining only supported claims: "Data engineer with 9 years of experience designing, building and operating production batch and streaming data platforms and cloud data warehouses across logistics, payments and retail." Keep the existing technology and reliability sentence, and add: "Experienced in optimising large-scale warehouse workloads, data quality and dimensional modelling." This is supported by the 1.2 TB daily EMR workload, 30 million events per day, dbt build-time reduction, and Snowflake cost reduction.
2. In the Senior Data Engineer section under Lukovac Freight Hub, revise the first bullet to make operational ownership more ATS-visible: "Own ingestion and orchestration for a production data platform, including approximately 140 Airflow DAGs loading data from PostgreSQL, MySQL, Salesforce and third-party APIs into Snowflake; participate in the data-platform on-call rotation one week in six." This uses evidence already present in the candidate notes and improves alignment with the responsibility to run a central platform.
3. In the Senior Data Engineer section under Lukovac Freight Hub, add the supported query-optimisation and scale evidence to the dbt or Snowflake bullet. For example, revise the dbt bullet to: "Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to dbt, building over 420 models with tests on every model; introduced incremental models and slim CI in GitHub Actions, reducing the nightly warehouse build from 5h 10m to 1h 35m." Then revise the Snowflake bullet to: "Reduced monthly Snowflake costs by approximately 37% through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removal of unused tables." This makes the existing optimisation evidence easier for ATS and recruiters to identify without claiming unsupported query techniques.
4. In the Skills section, change "Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling, data contracts, data quality testing" to "Data modelling and quality: Dimensional modelling (star schema), data contracts, data quality testing, JSON Schema". The star-schema wording is supported by the Redshift warehouse experience, and JSON Schema is explicitly documented in the data-contract achievement.
5. In the Open Source and Community section, retain the Airflow provider contribution but include the technologies from the original candidate material: "Contributed two merged pull requests to a community Airflow provider, fixing a pagination bug and adding Python tests." This strengthens the job's open-source-practices match while remaining concise.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Hiring Team at Halden Pay,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position. I have nine years of experience building data platforms across logistics, payments and retail, and I am drawn to the role’s focus on a shared platform that teams can rely on rather than one-off pipelines.

At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration for our data platform, including approximately 140 Airflow DAGs loading into Snowflake, and participate in the on-call rotation. I migrated around 300 stored procedures to dbt, introducing incremental models and CI checks that helped reduce the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. I also introduced data contracts and CI checks between product and data teams, reducing broken-pipeline incidents from roughly nine to two per month.

Previously at Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark reconciliation jobs on AWS and designed a dimensional Redshift warehouse used by finance and risk. The reconciliation work reduced manual effort from about three days to four hours per month-end. I have also built an internal Python library used by four teams and contributed fixes and tests to a community Airflow provider. That combination of payments experience, cloud platform work and reusable tooling fits well with the work described at Halden Pay.

I enjoy making pipelines easier to understand and trust, and sharing what I learn: I mentor two engineers and run weekly data platform office hours. I would be glad to discuss how I could help your team build and operate its shared data platform.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm
